newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada dlr weakens after erratic overnight session.
newsitem.headline: Canada dlr weakens after erratic overnight session.

text.p: Canada's dollar opened slightly weaker in thin trading at C$1.3797 (US$0.7247) on Wednesday after heavy two-way activity overnight in overseas markets, traders said.
They said the currency broke through stop-loss orders as it strengthened early in the overnight session to C$1.3730 (US$0.7283) before weakening on heavy selling of Canadian bonds in London.
"The Americans were very big sellers of Canada," said Reid Farrill, corporate foreign exchange adviser for CIBC Wood Gundy.

Analysts said the Canada dollar was likely to continue sliding today as U.S. players return to a selling posture and markets refocus on the possibility of a U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate hike at the next FOMC meeting on May 20.
"Given current interest spreads, Canada will come under pressure going into the FOMC," one trader said.
Others feared that the Bre-X Minerals Ltd scandal could turn foreign investors off Canadian stocks and trigger a further sell-off of the currency.
Major U.S. newspapers, including the Wall Street Journal, ran stories yesterday critical of Canada's stock markets.

"Re-establishing the credibility of the Canadian equity markets in light of the Bre-X fiasco will be something akin to hypnotizing a bunch of chickens," one trader wrote in an early morning commentary.
Overseas, the Japanese yen strengthened against the U.S. dollar largely on a report that Japan, Germany and the United States had agreed on a joint effort to sell U.S. dollars for yen.
The Group of Seven (G7) nations said in Washington last week that exchange rates should reflect economic fundamentals and that excessive fluctuations were undesirable.
The intervention speculation inititiated a move to hold yen at the expense of both the U.S. and Canadian dollar, traders said.
The Canadian dollar fell to 90.27 yen from Tuesday's close of 90.94 and jumped to 1.3811 marks from Tuesday's 1.3780 marks.
